profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a for-profit public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded on public markets under the ticker NVDA. Its site describes the company as a developer of open AI models and deployment infrastructure, with a particular focus on what it calls agentic AI, meaning long-running, self-evolving AI agents capable of complex reasoning, multimodal understanding, and autonomous task completion. The site reports annual revenue of approximately $215.9 billion for the period ending January 25, 2026, as filed in a 10-K with the SEC under CIK 0001045810.

NVIDIA's primary AI model family tracked here is NVIDIA Nemotron, described on the company's site as a family of multimodal, open foundation models built for agentic workflows including reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and document understanding. The site highlights Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant designed for faster specialized task completion, and NeMo Switchyard as a routing component that directs workloads to appropriate models. NVIDIA also publishes training datasets, model weights, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the site describes as permissive and allowing commercial use without attribution. Separately, NVIDIA NIM is tracked as inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments, available via build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production use. Supporting tools mentioned on the site include NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, and compatibility with open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. Bryan Catanzaro, described as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site in connection with the vision behind Nemotron.

The held facts note 187 legal exposure entries associated with California, though no specific cases are recorded in the current data.
